chapitre.paragraphe: Explicit substitutions are a way to represent the process of substituting variables in expressions without losing the structure of the original expression. This approach allows for more efficient manipulation of expressions, particularly in the context of programming languages and type systems.

The concept of explicit substitutions was introduced by Abadi, Cardelli, Curien, and Lévy in their seminal paper. They explored how explicit substitutions can be used to enhance the expressiveness of programming languages and improve the efficiency of type checking and evaluation.

The call-by-need lambda calculus is a computational model that optimizes the evaluation of expressions by delaying the computation of certain values until they are actually needed. This approach can lead to significant performance improvements in functional programming languages.
Ariola, Felleisen, Maraist, Odersky, and Wadler introduced this model in their work, demonstrating how it can be applied to enhance the efficiency of functional programming languages.
